core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 2776-2789): the canonical map g_{n!}K_n -> g_{n!}Z tensor^L K is the derived adjoint of the unit map K_n -> g_n^{-1}g_{n!}Z tensor K_n; by the component formula its restriction to C_m is the direct sum over varphi : [n] -> [m] of f_varphi^{-1}K_n -> K_m, i.e., the direct sum of the simplicial transition maps; this is an isomorphism for all n exactly when the transition maps are isomorphisms, which is the definition of cartesianness.

Part (2) (lines 2791-2814): with the flatness assumption on the O(varphi), the same argument in the ringed setting - the map is the adjoint of the O_n-unit, its restriction to C_m is the direct sum of f_varphi^*K_n -> f_varphi^*O_n tensor_{O_m} K_m = K_m (the equality because f_varphi^*O_n = O_m for a morphism of ringed topoi), again the direct sum of the transition maps - so the same characterization holds for O-modules.
proof_roadmap: Identify the canonical map as the derived adjoint of the unit and compute its restriction to C_m.
Read off that the components are the simplicial transition maps, in both the additive and the ringed settings.
Conclude the equivalence with cartesianness componentwise.
difficulty_reason: Characterization lemma (statement 2751-2772, proof 2774-2814): both halves compute the canonical shriek-tensor map componentwise and find the direct sum of the transition maps, so the equivalence with cartesianness is definitional once the computation is displayed - and it is displayed in-span, using the component formulas of the shriek lemmas and the exactness of g_{n!}; the closing 'Thus the statement is clear' follows the displayed reduction. H2: two short structural computations.
